title: Oceania capitals three of four · The Melanesian capitals
edition: Oceania capitals · Four regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to the Oceania capitals, episode three of four. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
Three capitals of the larger Melanesian states: the Solomon Islands, Papua New Guinea and Vanuatu.

states.name: Honiara
lines: Honiara stands on the north coast of Guadalcanal, in the Solomon Islands.
It grew out of an American base after the Second World War, and Henderson Field, the airstrip fought over in 1942, is now its airport.
Remember Honiara as a wartime airstrip that became a capital, on the island where the Guadalcanal campaign was fought.

states.name: Port Moresby
lines: Port Moresby stands on the shore of the Coral Sea, on the south coast of New Guinea, in the country of Papua New Guinea.
Named in 1873 by Captain John Moresby for his father, Admiral Fairfax Moresby, it is one of the largest cities in the Pacific islands outside Australia and New Zealand.
Remember Port Moresby as the Coral Sea city named by an admiral's son, and the gateway to the highlands behind it.
states.transition: Let's bring Port Moresby into view.

states.name: Port Vila
lines: Port Vila lies on a harbour on the island of Efate, in the centre of the New Hebrides, now Vanuatu.
Until 1980 it was the capital of a colony ruled jointly by Britain and France, and Cyclone Pam badly damaged it in 2015.
Remember Port Vila as the shared Anglo-French capital, and the town Cyclone Pam broke in 2015.
states.transition: Let's bring Port Vila into view.

recap: Honiara stands on Guadalcanal in the north, Port Moresby on the Coral Sea in the west, and Port Vila on Efate in the south-east.
Remember the wartime airstrip that became a capital, the Coral Sea city named by an admiral's son, and the Anglo-French capital that Cyclone Pam broke.
